title: The Great Bow of Shiva
captions: The next morning, King Janaka welcomed Vishvamitra and the princes to his court. “How may I serve you, great sage?” he asked. “These princes wish to see your famous bow,” said Vishvamitra.
“This bow once belonged to Lord Shiva himself,” said Janaka. “The devas gave it to my ancestor, King Devarata, and our family has kept it and worshipped it ever since.”
“One day, as I was ploughing a field for a yajna, a baby girl rose up out of the earth,” said Janaka. “I named her Sita and raised her as my own dear daughter.”
“I promised that Sita would marry only a hero strong enough to string Shiva's bow. Many mighty kings came to try, but not one of them could even lift it.”
Then Janaka gave an order. Five thousand strong men pulled the great bow into the hall, lying in an iron chest on eight wheels.
“Rama, look at this bow,” said Vishvamitra. Rama opened the chest and lifted the bow as if it were easy. Thousands watched in silence as he bent it and tied the string.
Rama drew the string back to his ear, and the mighty bow broke in two with a sound like thunder! The earth shook and people fell down. Only the sage, the king and the two princes stood firm.
story: The next morning, King Janaka welcomed Vishvamitra and the princes to his court and asked how he could serve them. Vishvamitra said the princes wished to see his famous bow.
Janaka explained that the bow had once belonged to Lord Shiva himself. The devas had given it to his ancestor, King Devarata, and the family had kept it and worshipped it ever since.

Then he told the story of his daughter. One day, as he was ploughing a field for a yajna, a baby girl rose up from the earth. He named her Sita and raised her as his own dear daughter. He promised that she would marry only a hero strong enough to string Shiva's bow. Many mighty kings had come to try, but none could even lift it.
Janaka gave an order, and five thousand strong men pulled the great bow into the hall. It lay in an iron chest on eight wheels. The whole court went quiet.

Vishvamitra asked Rama to look at the bow. Rama opened the chest and lifted the bow as if it were easy. He bent it and tied the string, and when he drew the string back to his ear, the mighty bow broke in two with a sound like thunder. The earth shook and people fell down. Only the sage, the king and the two princes stood firm.
lesson: Many mighty kings had failed to even lift Shiva's bow, yet Rama did not rush forward or boast. He waited for his guru's word, then calmly did what no one else could, and he stayed steady even when the bow broke with a sound like thunder. In our tradition, Dhairya means steady courage: a brave heart that stays calm when things are hard or frightening. Our elders teach that true courage is quiet and humble, and grows from a peaceful mind.
lesson_long: Dhairya means steady courage: a brave heart that stays calm when things are hard or frightening.

Many famous kings had failed, and the whole court was watching. Rama did not rush forward or boast. He waited for his guru's word, then calmly did what no one else could. When the bow broke with a sound like thunder, he stayed steady.
Our elders teach that true courage is quiet and humble. It grows from a peaceful mind, not from showing off.
tradition: The name Sita comes from the Sanskrit word for the line a plough makes in the earth. Because she rose from the earth, she is also called Bhumija, daughter of the earth, and Janaki, daughter of Janaka. Her birthday is celebrated as Sita Navami.
In many tellings, Lord Shiva's bow is called Pinaka, and Shiva himself is sometimes called Pinakapani, the one who holds Pinaka.
words: the name often given to Lord Shiva's bow
question: When you have to do something hard or a little scary, what helps you stay calm and brave?
questions: When you have to do something hard or a little scary, what helps you stay calm and brave?
Why do you think Rama waited for his guru before lifting the bow?
Can someone be brave and still feel a little scared inside?
card_lesson: Many kings had failed, but Rama stayed calm. He waited for his guru's word and lifted the bow with a steady heart. Dhairya means courage that stays calm and steady.
